# Accepted dependency risk — register and due dates

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/check_suppressions.py --markdown. Do not edit by hand;
     regenerate after changing osv-scanner.toml. A test compares this file with
     the live config, so a stale table fails CI rather than misleads a reader. -->

Every entry in `osv-scanner.toml` is debt with a due date. When an `effectiveUntil` passes, osv-scanner stops honouring the acceptance and the finding returns to CI — there is no silent ageing. This table exists so the next one can be seen coming. Run `python scripts/check_suppressions.py` for the live countdown; this file records only what does not change daily.

## Rotation

Each row needs one of two outcomes before its date: an upgrade that closes the advisory, or a fresh argument written into the entry's `reason` plus a new `effectiveUntil`. Extending a date without re-arguing it is the failure mode this register is meant to make visible.

`scripts/check_suppressions.py` (run by `tests/test_suppressions.py`) fails the build if an entry no longer maps to a package, or if the package is already pinned past the advisory's fixed version — both were true of 13 of the 20 entries removed on 2026-11-18.
